rationale: Source reading plus construction in a scratch copy supports fixing one attributed responsibility for this Candidate. installSnapshot installs the remote snapshot, sets lastApplied/lastSnapshot and, for a monotonic LogStore, calls removeOldLogs which deletes every log entry, but it never updates the cached last log identity; the sibling leader-side restoreUserSnapshot does call setLastLog for exactly this reason, and the MonotonicLogStore contract states the reset is required when gaps are not allowed. The composed requirement is that after a snapshot install the node's reported and compared last log entry must be re-derived (or the cache updated) so the follower can accept the leader's post-install AppendEntries. The claim is bounded to that recovery path with a monotonic store, excludes the non-monotonic path and the at-or-below-snapshot case, and is offered as ready_for_check; construction showed the emptied store with a cached index of 5 and snapshot index 2 rejecting the follow-up AppendEntries, but formal evidence requires the trusted runner.

question.question: When a follower with a monotonic LogStore installs a remote snapshot whose index is below the follower's cached last log index, installSnapshot empties the log store (removeOldLogs) and sets lastSnapshot but never updates the cached last log identity; does the follower then report and compare a last log entry that no longer exists, so that it rejects every subsequent AppendEntries and keeps looping on snapshots instead of catching up - or does some other mechanism re-derive the identity?
question.importance: A follower that cannot accept AppendEntries after a snapshot install cannot resynchronize: its cached last log index/term feed AppendEntriesResponse.LastLog, the RequestVote up-to-date comparison and the PrevLog decision inside appendEntries, so a divergence can keep the node permanently behind, withholding its participation in quorum and (for enough stuck voters) costing availability. The entries involved are uncommitted, so the concern is bounded liveness and recovery, not consensus safety or data loss.
contexts: Follower main goroutine handling an InstallSnapshot RPC while its cached last log index is above the incoming snapshot index
Injected LogStore that implements MonotonicLogStore with IsMonotonic() true, so the install path calls removeOldLogs instead of compactLogs
A leader that, after a successful install, sets the follower's nextIndex to snapshotIndex+1 and sends AppendEntries from there
event_paths: InstallSnapshot -> version/term checks -> snapshot sink created, copied and closed -> fsmMutateCh restore -> setLastApplied/setLastSnapshot -> removeOldLogs deletes all log entries -> lastLogIndex/lastLogTerm unchanged
leader sendLatestSnapshot success -> atomic.StoreUint64(&s.nextIndex, meta.Index+1) and commitment.match(peer.ID, meta.Index)
next AppendEntries with PrevLogEntry=meta.Index -> r.getLastEntry() uses the stale cached index above the snapshot index -> PrevLogTerm mismatch -> reject
later AppendEntries entries at indexes <= stale cached index -> r.getLastLog() used for classification -> r.logs.GetLog returns ErrLogNotFound on the emptied store -> reject
leader consumes resp.LastLog (getLastIndex = stale cache) -> s.nextIndex decremented until the leader's own log no longer covers it -> sendLatestSnapshot again

supporting_behavior_ids.B-snapshot-install: Cause/context: installSnapshot installs the snapshot, sets lastSnapshot/lastApplied and, for a monotonic LogStore, removes all log entries without updating the cached last log identity - the mechanism that can separate the cache from the store.

counterevidence: For a non-monotonic LogStore the install path calls compactLogs(req.LastLogIndex), which retains trailing entries, so the cached last log index stays consistent with the store

When the follower's cached last log index is at or below the snapshot index, getLastEntry and getLastIndex take the maximum of the log and snapshot values, so the PrevLog identity matches and the entries block appends from the lower cached index
installSnapshot does set lastApplied and lastSnapshot to the incoming index, so getLastEntry/getLastIndex of an empty-log follower still reflect the snapshot
The leader sets nextIndex to snapshotIndex+1 after a successful install, so any subsequent successful StoreLogs on the follower calls setLastLog and repairs the cache
unknowns: Whether a follower's cached last log index can exceed the leader's chosen snapshot index in a legal history (for example a previous leader's uncommitted suffix), which is what makes the emptied store diverge from the cache
Whether the resulting PrevLog/GetLog rejections terminate through a snapshot resend plus successful store, or repeat indefinitely with the cache never updated
Whether the divergence is confined to monotonic LogStore implementations and how common those are among caller-supplied stores
question.trigger_rationale: The install path contains two facts that are not obviously compatible: installSnapshot never calls setLastLog, while the sibling leader-side restore path does, and the monotonic-store branch deletes all logs rather than retaining trailing ones. The MonotonicLogStore contract itself says the store must support removing all logs after snapshot restore, so the emptied store is intended; whether the cached identity is then re-derived is what stays unstated. Because the index relationship between the follower's cache and the leader's snapshot is not fixed by the code, the case needs to be isolated and, if reachable, executed.

obligation.description: When a follower installs a remote snapshot whose index is below its cached last log index and its LogStore is monotonic (IsMonotonic true, so installSnapshot resets the log store), the node must re-derive or update its cached last log identity so that the leader's subsequent AppendEntries from the snapshot index are accepted; leaving the cache naming entries the emptied store no longer holds must not make the follower reject recovery replication indefinitely.

scope.description: Follower main goroutine handling a valid InstallSnapshot RPC while raftState.lastLogIndex is above the incoming snapshot index and the injected LogStore implements MonotonicLogStore with IsMonotonic() true.
assumptions: The InstallSnapshot request is legal: supported snapshot version, term not older than currentTerm, size matching the streamed bytes.
The LogStore faithfully implements the LogStore interface and reports IsMonotonic() true, so the install path calls removeOldLogs.
The leader continues to replicate from snapshotIndex+1 after a successful install (as sendLatestSnapshot does).
excluded: Non-monotonic LogStores, where installSnapshot calls compactLogs and keeps trailing entries
The case where the cached last log index is at or below the snapshot index, which the max() in getLastEntry/getLastIndex already covers
Consensus safety or data loss: the discarded entries are uncommitted

pending: A monotonic-store follower scenario that installs a snapshot below its cached last log index and then observes both the cached identity and the acceptance of the leader's follow-up AppendEntries.

grounding.derivation: installSnapshot sets lastApplied and lastSnapshot from the request and then, for a monotonic LogStore, calls removeOldLogs, which deletes every log entry (S-raft-installsnapshot, S-logstore-monotonic). It never calls setLastLog, whereas the sibling leader-side restoreUserSnapshot does. The last log identity is consumed by getLastEntry for the PrevLog comparison and by getLastLog in the entries-classification loop of appendEntries (S-raft-appendentries), so an emptied store combined with a stale cache makes the follower reject the entries the leader sends from the snapshot index; the leader's sendLatestSnapshot sets nextIndex to snapshotIndex+1 on success (S-replication), which is exactly the request that gets rejected.
grounding.applicability: Applies to the follower install handler under the monotonic-store and above-snapshot-index premises above; it asserts no obligation for non-monotonic stores, for a cache at or below the snapshot index, or for the quorum protocol.
unresolved: Whether a legal history produces a cached last log index above the leader's chosen snapshot index.
Whether the rejection loop terminates through a later successful store or repeats with the cache never updated.
alternatives: A cache at or below the snapshot index is rescued by the maximum of log and snapshot values, so the failure requires the cache to exceed the snapshot index.

associations.rationale: This is the branch that empties the log store while the cached last log identity remains unchanged, which is the divergence the claim forbids.

bindings.description: The monotonic-store branch of installSnapshot that calls removeOldLogs (deleting all log entries) instead of compactLogs, immediately after lastSnapshot/lastApplied are set and without any setLastLog call.
pending: Whether removeOldLogs ever fails for the injected store.
